Arnault began his career in 1971, at [Ferret-Savinel](/wiki/Nexity "Nexity"), and was its president from 1978 to 1984.[[8]](#cite_note-France24-9)[[12]](#cite_note-NYT_2007-13) In 1984, Arnault, then a young real estate developer, heard that the French government was set to choose someone to take over the Boussac Saint-Frères empire, a textile and retail conglomerate that owned [Christian Dior](/wiki/Dior "Dior").[[15]](#cite_note-:0-16)

With the help of Antoine Bernheim, a senior partner of [Lazard](/wiki/Lazard "Lazard") Frères, Arnault acquired the [Financière Agache](/wiki/Financi%C3%A8re_Agache "Financière Agache"), a [luxury goods](/wiki/Luxury_goods "Luxury goods") company.[[16]](#cite_note-:4-17) He became the CEO of Financière Agache and subsequently won the bidding war for Boussac Saint-Frères, buying the group for a ceremonial one franc and effectively taking control of Boussac Saint-Frères. After Arnault bought Boussac, he laid off 9,000 workers in two years, after which he acquired the nickname "The Terminator".[[15]](#cite_note-:0-16) He sold nearly all of the company's assets, keeping only the Christian Dior brand and Le Bon Marché department store. By 1987, the company was profitable again and booked earnings of $112 million on a revenue stream of $1.9 billion.[[16]](#cite_note-:4-17)

On most windows, the start of the [title bar](/wiki/Title_bar "Title bar") has three buttons resembling a horizontal [traffic light](/wiki/Traffic_light "Traffic light"), which respectively close, minimize, and resize the window.

Apple has continued to change aspects of the macOS appearance and design, particularly with tweaks to the appearance of windows and the menu bar. Since 2012, Apple has sold almost all of its Mac models with high-resolution [Retina displays](/wiki/Retina_display "Retina display"), and macOS and its [APIs](/wiki/Application_programming_interface "Application programming interface") have extensive support for resolution-independent development on supporting high-resolution displays. Reviewers have described Apple's support for the technology as superior to that on Windows.[[136]](#cite_note-141)[[137]](#cite_note-142)[[138]](#cite_note-143)

The [human interface guidelines](/wiki/Human_interface_guidelines "Human interface guidelines") published by Apple for macOS are followed by many applications, giving them consistent user interface and keyboard shortcuts.[[139]](#cite_note-144) Services available in every Cocoa application include spelling and grammar checkers, special characters palette, color picker, font chooser and dictionary. The **epidemiology of cancer** is the study of the factors affecting [cancer](/wiki/Cancer "Cancer"), as a way to infer possible trends and causes. This area of study must contend with problems of [lead time bias](/wiki/Lead_time_bias "Lead time bias") and [length time bias](/wiki/Length_time_bias "Length time bias"). Lead time bias is the concept that early diagnosis may artificially inflate the survival statistics of a cancer, without really improving the natural history of the disease. Length bias is the concept that slower growing, more indolent tumors are more likely to be diagnosed by screening tests, but improvements in diagnosing more cases of indolent cancer may not translate into better patient outcomes after the implementation of screening programs.
